record.paper_title: Two open problems in graph theory
record.original_question: A graph is hypohamiltonian if it is not hamiltonian but every vertex-deleted subgraph is hamiltonian. For which integers n does there exist a hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices? In particular, does such a graph exist on 17 vertices?

evidence.quote: If Gi is not hamiltonian and Gv is hamiltonian for all v € VG, then G is said to be hypohamiltonian.
Given that we know there are an infinite number of hypohamiltonian graphs, a natural question to ask is, "Is there a hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices for every value of n?"

No-one has yet produced a hypohamiltonian graph of order 17. Given the existence of hypohamiltonian graphs for n = 15,16 and n > 18, there seems to be a good chance that there is one for n = 17. But, of course, there might not be!

artifact.self_contained_problem: A simple graph G is called hypohamiltonian if G itself does not contain a Hamiltonian cycle, but for every vertex v of G the vertex-deleted subgraph G − v does contain a Hamiltonian cycle. Determine the set of positive integers n for which there exists a hypohamiltonian graph on n vertices. In particular, decide whether a hypohamiltonian graph on exactly 17 vertices exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The order spectrum of hypohamiltonian graphs is now completely known. Such graphs exist precisely for n = 10, 13, 15, 16, and for every n ≥ 18; no hypohamiltonian graph exists for n ∈ {3,…,9, 11, 12, 14, 17}. In particular, the existence question for n = 17 has been settled negatively via exhaustive computer enumeration (Aldred–McKay–Wormald and subsequent verifications).

status_evidence.title: Hypohamiltonian graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: A complete list of hypohamiltonian graphs with at most 17 vertices is known: they are the 10-vertex Petersen graph, a 13-vertex graph and a 15-vertex graph found by computer searches of Herz (1968), and four 16-vertex graphs. ... such graphs exist for all n ≥ 18.
status_evidence.claim: There is no hypohamiltonian graph on 17 vertices, and the order spectrum is fully determined.

status_evidence.title: Small planar hypohamiltonian graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work continues to extend known catalogues of hypohamiltonian graphs and confirms the established order spectrum.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent literature treats the order spectrum as known, with focus shifted to refinements such as planarity.
